prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Production asset: a transparent PNG sprite atlas for an existing top-down 2.5D fantasy pixel-art RPG forest. Create a NEW original set of environmental props, designed to blend into hand-painted pixel terrain with chunky mossy leaf shapes. Square 2048x2048 canvas, exactly FOUR COLUMNS and FOUR ROWS, sixteen isolated objects with ample transparent gutters, each centered in its own equal cell; no labels, grid lines, background, ground tiles, or text. Genuine transparent background.
ROW ONE from left: 1 full green broadleaf tree with rounded asymmetric crown, 2 old spreading oak with a low fork and broad layered canopy, 3 tall full pine with broad overlapping needles grouped in several big tiers, 4 graceful green willow with hanging broad curtains of leaves.
ROW TWO: 1 upright airy broadleaf tree with separated crown clusters, 2 leaning oak with crooked trunk and windward canopy, 3 open irregular pine with visible gaps between five broad branch tiers, 4 forked dead oak with broken limbs and a little moss.
ROW THREE: 1 squat gray moss-covered boulder group, 2 low leafy forest shrub, 3 moss-covered fallen log angled mildly, 4 rooted old stump.
ROW FOUR: 1 short broken ancient gray limestone column stump encased by moss and a few roots, 2 bent dead tree with a snapped high branch, 3 low sloping broad mossy stone slab, 4 a low graceful fern cluster.
Style is game pixel painting with explicit crisp stepped edges and hand-placed color clusters. Trees must have large readable crowns built out of 5-9 principal leaf masses and 3-4 broad shading planes, sparse selected leaf details. Match warm olive and moss greens, muted brown-gray trunks, warm upper-left daylight and green underside shadows. NOT photorealistic, NOT delicate stippling or thousands of tiny leaves, NOT a bonsai miniature. Avoid black outlines, shiny leaves, blur and gradients, long orange roots, too-dark tree interior and tiny dense leaf noise. The illustration should stay cohesive when shrunk to 100-160 pixels high in the game. Objects have a high oblique top-down game view: some crown tops and rock top surfaces visible, trunks vertical. Each tree silhouette must be clearly different, no repeated crowns. All trees have only a small asymmetrical low moss/root footing, no isolated circular pedestal and no large cast-shadow disc. Small props drawn at an appropriately larger scale within their cells so they crop cleanly. Complete trunks/feet/crowns inside each cell, no touching adjacent sprites. No flowers/fruits, no decorative glowing particles.
